title: REMORY: Learning Residual Memory for Context Compaction

beats.text: Why do 50% of your GPU cycles waste compute before REMORY fixes the bottleneck?
beats.visual_focus: A blueprint fading into a pile of rubble

beats.text: The villain is the 'Summary Gap'. Textual summaries lose the structural integrity required for complex, long-horizon decision making.
beats.visual_focus: A data stream snapping under pressure

beats.text: Enter REMORY. It treats memory as a residual connection, splicing soft tokens directly after the summary to restore latent signals.
The network generates these tokens conditioned on the summary, acting as a frozen LLM's missing link to the full history.

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: The hook was solid—I hate hitting context limits, so you had me immediately. I like that you didn't use 'AI magic' metaphors. However, 'splice soft tokens' felt a bit hand-wavy. I get that you're injecting latent signals, but are you literally concatenating these to the KV cache or just prepending them to the input sequence? A tiny bit more technical precision there would make me trust the mechanism more.
